checkpoint_review: The Router correctly identified that the majority of the diagnostic checkpoints (exterior walls, towers, grounds) are not testable due to the interior perspective of the image. This is a valid application of the 'is_testable' rule. The Router accurately marked the visible features (barred gate, stone construction, utilitarian style) as present. I agree with all verdicts; the Router was neither too lenient nor too strict.
artifact_review: The Router found no artifacts. The experts largely supported this: the topology auditor confirmed the gate's structural integrity (high mask confidence), and the depth auditor found no spatial warping. However, the perceptual quality auditor flagged the image as 'darken' with 'serious' severity. While the image is high-contrast and moody (intentional for a prison scene), the shadows are indeed very deep, potentially losing detail. I will slightly penalize the artifact score for this lighting issue, but not severely, as it fits the aesthetic context. No structural melting or fusion was detected in the bars or walls.
alignment_reasoning: The fine-grained classifier strongly confirms the class 'prison' (logit 7.23 vs 2.62 for next best). The visible elements (barred gate, stone tunnel) are highly characteristic of the class. Although many exterior checkpoints were N/A, the interior cues are sufficient for strong alignment.
artifact_reasoning: Structural integrity is high (gate bars are straight and distinct). Depth map shows valid perspective. The primary defect is the 'darken' classification by the perceptual auditor; while stylistically appropriate, the extreme contrast results in some loss of shadow detail, preventing a perfect 5.0 artifact score.
